analyst_view.overall: Early view: a relegation six-pointer between 16th and 18th. Osasuna changed coach in October, Jagoba Arrasate replacing Luis Miguel Ramis, and rescued a 1-1 against Athletic in stoppage time, with Herrando, Oroz and Del Castillo expected back after the break; Martín Anselmi's Elche have yet to win at home but did win 0-3 at Rayo, and Lemar is out until late November.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Osasuna have conceded 23 in 12, which argues for goals, but Elche have scored once in their last three games and Anselmi admits they are not converting chances. I stay around 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Elche are a possession side (69% at home to Valencia) and their game with Betis produced 17 corners, while Osasuna's equaliser against Athletic came from a corner. I lean higher, around 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards. Osasuna picked up three and four yellows in their last two games and Elche four against Betis, in a game with relegation stakes; Moncayola is one yellow away from a ban rather than suspended. I lean slightly higher, around 5-6.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots. Osasuna's last home game had 33 shots and Elche have taken 13-16 shots in each of their last two games despite not scoring. I lean slightly higher, around 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 on target. Elche had only one shot on target from 13 against Betis and failed to score from 16 against Valencia, so their accuracy is the weak point. I lean lower, around 7.
